result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A says plainly that the numbers don't show the program worked, and it is the only answer that suggests re-testing or observing agents a few weeks later on realistic cases. Its four-step plan and director script also fit a small team. B gives richer real-work metrics and is more candid about n=12 and early results being directional, but it suggests five measures plus blinded manager ratings, which is heavier than needed. Its only knowledge check runs at the start and end of the course, with no check weeks later. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the numbers don't show the program worked, and both give the director usable wording. B is better because it explicitly calls for re-testing agents a few weeks later on realistic cases and keeps the plan short. A offers a longer list of measures, and its only knowledge check is at the start and end of the course. Both slightly overclaim that agents 'learned the content'. A names the small sample size, but its director script then says 'the content is landing' even though it had just said the 91% means little without a baseline.
